chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from his father who said:
I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the enema which a person inserts while he is fasting?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'There is no problem with the solids.'

key_terms.التَّلَطُّف: Enema or insertion of medicine into the rectum

ai.seo_question: Does an enema break the fast in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the fiqh of fasting by distinguishing between solid and liquid substances introduced into the body, ruling that a solid enema (*jamid*) does not break the fast. This ruling reflects the scholarly principle that the fast is primarily invalidated by the consumption of food and drink, and by extension, liquids that reach the stomach, whereas solids or non-nutritive substances may be treated differently depending on their nature and absorption. The hadith highlights the precision in Shia jurisprudence regarding the physical integrity of the fast during medical or hygienic procedures.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Husayn, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from his father who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the enema which the human being has inserted and he is Fasting’. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘There is no problem with the solids’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from his father who has said the following: “I once wrote to abu al-Hassan and asked about one’s performing an enema when fasting. He (the Imam) wrote back, ‘It is not harmful with a solid substance (as opposed to liquid).”’
